children.title: Hybrid Conjugate-Gradient Coefficients
children.top_down_role: Combinations that switch or blend established nonlinear conjugate-gradient coefficients.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Conjugate-Gradient Coefficients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic safeguarded hybridization of two nonlinear conjugate-gradient coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable, let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and let \(y_{k-1}=g_k-g_{k-1}\). Given two defined base coefficients \(\beta_k^{(1)}\) and \(\beta_k^{(2)}\), a hybrid coefficient is \[\beta_k^{\mathrm{hyb}}=\Pi_{[\ell_k,u_k]}\!\left((1-\lambda_k)\beta_k^{(1)}+\lambda_k\beta_k^{(2)}\right),\qquad 0\leq\lambda_k\leq1,\] where \(\ell_k\leq u_k\) and \(\Pi_{[\ell_k,u_k]}(t)=\min\{u_k,\max\{\ell_k,t\}\}\). The associated direction is \(d_k=-g_k+\beta_k^{\mathrm{hyb}}d_{k-1}\), with \(d_0=-g_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid coefficient is a safeguarded convex combination of two admissible conjugate-gradient coefficients, used in the standard two-term search-direction recurrence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_k=-g_k+\beta_k^{\mathrm{hyb}}d_{k-1}\) defines the corresponding safeguarded hybrid direction.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection of a scalar onto an interval.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the coefficient leaf, but the safeguarded convex-combination formula is only a generic construction and is not tied to an identified hybrid conjugate-gradient family. The plain statement additionally calls the base coefficients admissible, whereas the mathematical statement assumes only that they are defined.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameterized Conjugate-Gradient Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scalar-parameter family interpolating nonlinear conjugate-gradient recurrences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\) and \(d_0=-g_0\). For \(k\geq0\), choose a line-search step \(\alpha_k>0\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and compute \(g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1})\). For prescribed endpoint formulas \(B_{k+1}^{(0)}\) and \(B_{k+1}^{(1)}\), choose \(\tau_{k+1}\in[0,1]\) and define \[\beta_{k+1}(\tau_{k+1})=(1-\tau_{k+1})B_{k+1}^{(0)}+\tau_{k+1}B_{k+1}^{(1)},\qquad d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}(\tau_{k+1})d_k.\] Stop when a specified gradient-norm tolerance is met; otherwise output the last iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The family interpolates between two conjugate-gradient coefficient formulas through a scalar parameter and inserts the result into the usual direction recurrence.
assumptions_latex: The endpoint coefficients are defined whenever used
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure generates a parameterized family of nonlinear conjugate-gradient iterates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is an appropriate kind, but unspecified endpoint formulas make this an arbitrary interpolation template rather than a source-supported parameterized conjugate-gradient family.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Selection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterationwise rules selecting between or blending candidate conjugate-gradient coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\beta_k^{(1)}\) and \(\beta_k^{(2)}\) be candidate coefficients and let \(D_k\subset\mathbb{R}\) be the set of coefficients satisfying the required safeguards at iteration \(k\), such as descent or boundedness tests. A hybrid selection regime chooses \[\beta_k\in D_k\cap\operatorname{conv}\{\beta_k^{(1)},\beta_k^{(2)}\}.\] Endpoint switching selects one candidate lying in \(D_k\); clipped blending selects \(\Pi_{D_k}((1-\lambda_k)\beta_k^{(1)}+\lambda_k\beta_k^{(2)})\) when \(D_k\) is a nonempty closed interval. If the intersection is empty, the regime restarts by setting \(\beta_k=0\), hence \(d_k=-g_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid regime selects a safeguarded endpoint or blend of candidate coefficients and restarts with steepest descent when no candidate is admissible.
assumptions_latex: The two candidate coefficients are finite
\(D_k\) is specified by the method's safeguards
Projection is used only when \(D_k\) is a nonempty closed interval
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected coefficient is admissible whenever the feasible intersection is nonempty; otherwise the rule produces a restart.

notation.meaning: Admissible coefficient set at iteration k.
Scalar projection onto the admissible interval.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition fits the leaf, but the clipped projection onto D_k need not remain in the convex hull of the two coefficients, so it does not necessarily satisfy the initially stated selection rule. A family-specific source and corrected regime are required.

children.title: Modified Conjugate-Gradient Recurrences

knowledge_statements.title: Modified Conjugate-Gradient Recurrences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic two-term recurrence augmented by a controlled correction vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\) and \(d_0=-g_0\). For \(k\geq0\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and compute \(g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1})\). Select a conjugate-gradient coefficient \(\beta_{k+1}\), a correction vector \(v_{k+1}\), and a modification parameter \(\eta_{k+1}\), then update \[d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k+\eta_{k+1}v_{k+1}.\] Accept the direction only if \(g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}d_{k+1}<0\); otherwise restart with \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}\). Stop at the prescribed gradient tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A modified recurrence adds a controlled correction vector to the ordinary conjugate-gradient direction and restarts whenever descent is lost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted or restarted direction satisfies \(g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}d_{k+1}<0\) when \(g_{k+1}\neq0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the recurrence leaf, but the arbitrary correction vector and weight do not identify the intended modified conjugate-gradient family. The displayed recurrence requires a source specifying these quantities.

children.title: Accelerated Conjugate-Gradient Variants

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Conjugate-Gradient Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extrapolated nonlinear conjugate-gradient template with a safeguarded direction recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0=x_{-1}\in\mathbb{R}^n\), choose \(t_0=1\), and set \(d_{-1}=0\). For \(k\geq0\), choose an extrapolation factor \(\theta_k\), form \(z_k=x_k+\theta_k(x_k-x_{k-1})\), and set \(g_k=\nabla f(z_k)\). Compute \(d_k=-g_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}\), replacing it by \(-g_k\) unless \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k<0\). Choose \(\alpha_k>0\) by line search from \(z_k\), set \(x_{k+1}=z_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and update the acceleration state, for example \(t_{k+1}=(1+\sqrt{1+4t_k^2})/2\) and \(\theta_{k+1}=(t_k-1)/t_{k+1}\). Stop at the prescribed stationarity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An accelerated variant extrapolates the iterate before forming a safeguarded conjugate-gradient direction and taking a line-search step.
assumptions_latex: The coefficient \(\beta_k\) is defined at each iteration
The line search returns a positive step
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The template produces extrapolated iterates with descent directions at each accepted line-search call.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the variants leaf, but combining a Nesterov-style state update with a nonlinear conjugate-gradient recurrence is family-specific and unsupported here. The coefficient and admissible extrapolation regime are also unspecified.

children.title: Modification Robustness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Curvature and line-search regimes where modified recurrences lose their intended benefit.

knowledge_statements.title: Modification Robustness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp iterationwise descent boundary for additive direction modifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the unmodified direction \(p_k\) satisfy \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k\leq-c\lVert g_k\rVert^2\) for some \(c>0\), and let the modified direction be \(d_k=p_k+e_k\). If \(\lVert e_k\rVert\leq\rho\lVert g_k\rVert\) with \(0\leq\rho<c\), then \[g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\leq-(c-\rho)\lVert g_k\rVert^2<0\qquad\text{whenever }g_k\neq0.\] The threshold is sharp under only this norm bound: when \(\rho\geq c\), choosing \(p_k=-c g_k\) and \(e_k=\rho g_k\) yields \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k=(\rho-c)\lVert g_k\rVert^2\geq0\), so descent may fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An additive modification preserves sufficient descent when its relative norm is below the descent margin; at or above that margin, a parallel perturbation can destroy descent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Descent is guaranteed for \(\rho<c\) and is not guaranteed for \(\rho\geq c\).

knowledge_statements.title: Three-Term Conjugate Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonlinear conjugate-gradient directions with two carried vector components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\) and \(d_0=-g_0\). For \(k\geq0\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and define \(g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1})\) and \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\). Select scalar coefficients \(\beta_{k+1}\) and \(\gamma_{k+1}\), then form the three-term direction \[d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k+\gamma_{k+1}y_k.\] If a prescribed descent safeguard fails, set \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}\). Stop when \(\lVert g_k\rVert\) meets the requested tolerance and output \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Three-term nonlinear conjugate gradient augments the negative gradient and previous direction with a third component, commonly the gradient difference.
assumptions_latex: The coefficient formulas are defined whenever used
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recurrence generates directions containing the additional component \(y_k\), with restart available to enforce descent.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Nonlinear Conjugate Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonlinear conjugate gradient with a positive scalar scaling of the gradient component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\), choose \(\sigma_0>0\), and let \(d_0=-\sigma_0g_0\). For \(k\geq0\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\) by line search, set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and compute \(g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1})\). Choose a scale \(\sigma_{k+1}>0\) and a conjugate-gradient coefficient \(\beta_{k+1}\), then set \[d_{k+1}=-\sigma_{k+1}g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k.\] Restart with \(d_{k+1}=-\sigma_{k+1}g_{k+1}\) if the proposed direction fails the selected descent test; stop at the prescribed gradient tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled nonlinear conjugate gradient multiplies the negative-gradient component by a positive iteration-dependent scalar while retaining the conjugate-gradient memory term.
assumptions_latex: The line search returns a positive step
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method generates scaled nonlinear conjugate-gradient directions and can restart to a scaled steepest-descent direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioned Nonlinear Conjugate Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed positive-definite preconditioning applied to nonlinear conjugate-gradient residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite. Given \(x_0\), compute \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\), solve \(Mz_0=g_0\), and set \(d_0=-z_0\). After choosing \(\alpha_k>0\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), compute \(g_{k+1}\), and solve \(Mz_{k+1}=g_{k+1}\). One preconditioned Polak--Ribiere recurrence is \[\beta_{k+1}=\frac{g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}(z_{k+1}-z_k)}{g_k^{\mathsf T}z_k},\qquad d_{k+1}=-z_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k.\] Restart with \(-z_{k+1}\) when the denominator vanishes or the direction fails the prescribed descent test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preconditioned nonlinear conjugate gradient replaces the raw gradient by the solution of a positive-definite preconditioning system and uses it in the recurrence.
assumptions_latex: The coefficient is used only when \(g_k^{\mathsf T}z_k>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recurrence defines a fixed-metric preconditioned nonlinear conjugate-gradient method.

children.title: Conjugacy Under Metric Changes
children.top_down_role: Effects of scaling or metric variation on direction quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugacy Under Metric Changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact preservation criterion for pairwise conjugacy when the defining metric changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_k,M_{k+1}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive-definite matrices and define \(\langle u,v\rangle_{M}=u^{\mathsf T}Mv\). If two nonzero directions \(d_i,d_j\) are conjugate in metric \(M_k\), so \(d_i^{\mathsf T}M_kd_j=0\), then they remain conjugate in metric \(M_{k+1}\) if and only if \[d_i^{\mathsf T}(M_{k+1}-M_k)d_j=0.\] Consequently, arbitrary positive-definite metric changes need not preserve previously established conjugacy; preservation requires the metric perturbation to vanish on every relevant cross-pair of stored directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directions conjugate in one metric remain conjugate after a metric change exactly when the metric perturbation has zero cross-product on those directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_i^{\mathsf T}M_{k+1}d_j=0\) if and only if \(d_i^{\mathsf T}(M_{k+1}-M_k)d_j=0\).

notation.meaning: Inner product induced by a positive-definite matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Wolfe Globalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong-Wolfe line search applied to nonlinear conjugate-gradient directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<c_1<c_2<1\). Given \(x_k\), gradient \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and a descent direction \(d_k\) satisfying \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k<0\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\) such that \[f(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\leq f(x_k)+c_1\alpha_kg_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\] and \[\left|\nabla f(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)^{\mathsf T}d_k\right|\leq c_2\left|g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\right|.\] Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), compute the selected nonlinear conjugate-gradient coefficient, and form the next direction; restart with \(-g_{k+1}\) whenever the proposed direction is not descent. Stop at the prescribed gradient tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong-Wolfe globalization accepts a step only when sufficient decrease and absolute curvature conditions hold, with restart if the next conjugate-gradient direction is not descent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each accepted step satisfies both strong-Wolfe inequalities before the nonlinear conjugate-gradient recurrence continues.

children.title: Sufficient-Descent Modifications
children.top_down_role: Direction and coefficient modifications preserving descent.

knowledge_statements.title: Sufficient-Descent Modifications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fallback modification enforcing uniform descent in nonlinear conjugate-gradient iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a differentiable objective \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), an iterate \(x_k\), gradient \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), previous direction \(d_{k-1}\), tentative coefficient \(\widehat\beta_k\), and constant \(c\in(0,1]\), form \(\widehat d_k=-g_k+\widehat\beta_k d_{k-1}\). Set \[d_k=\begin{cases}\widehat d_k,&g_k^{\mathsf T}\widehat d_k\le -c\lVert g_k\rVert^2,\\-g_k,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}\] Choose a positive line-search step \(\alpha_k\) and update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_k d_k\). Stop when a prescribed gradient tolerance is met. Every accepted direction satisfies \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\le-c\lVert g_k\rVert^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept the conjugate-gradient direction only when it provides uniform sufficient descent; otherwise restart with steepest descent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\le-c\lVert g_k\rVert^2<0\).

children.title: Conjugate-Gradient Restart Trigger Family
children.top_down_role: Scheduled and geometry-triggered returns to steepest descent.

children.title: Periodic Conjugate-Gradient Restarts
children.top_down_role: Scheduled returns to steepest-descent directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Periodic Conjugate-Gradient Restarts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-frequency restart rule for nonlinear conjugate-gradient recurrences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an integer period \(m\ge1\). Initialize \(d_0=-g_0\), where \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\). For each \(k\ge1\), compute a tentative coefficient \(\widehat\beta_k\) and set \[\beta_k=\begin{cases}0,&k\equiv0\pmod m,\\\widehat\beta_k,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\qquad d_k=-g_k+\beta_k d_{k-1}.\] Choose \(\alpha_k>0\) by the prescribed line search and update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). Thus every index divisible by \(m\) uses \(d_k=-g_k\), and no block of \(m\) consecutive generated directions contains fewer than one scheduled restart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set the conjugacy coefficient to zero every fixed number of iterations, thereby periodically replacing the recurrence by steepest descent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k\equiv0\pmod m\) implies \(\beta_k=0\) and \(d_k=-g_k\).

children.title: Orthogonality-Triggered Restarts
children.top_down_role: Geometry-based restarts activated by loss of gradient orthogonality.

knowledge_statements.title: Orthogonality-Triggered Restarts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Powell-type restart based on loss of successive-gradient orthogonality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose a threshold \(\tau\in(0,1)\), initialize \(d_0=-g_0\), and for \(k\ge1\) compute \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and a tentative coefficient \(\widehat\beta_k\). Define \[r_k=\frac{|g_k^{\mathsf T}g_{k-1}|}{\lVert g_k\rVert^2},\qquad \beta_k=\begin{cases}0,&r_k\ge\tau,\\\widehat\beta_k,&r_k<\tau,
\end{cases}\qquad d_k=-g_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}.\] If \(g_k=0\), terminate instead of evaluating \(r_k\). A triggered iteration therefore discards accumulated conjugacy information and uses the steepest-descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart whenever consecutive gradients fail a prescribed approximate-orthogonality test; at a restart, use the negative current gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_k\ge\tau\) implies \(\beta_k=0\) and \(d_k=-g_k\).

children.title: Restart Trigger Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs among scheduled and geometry-sensitive restart triggers.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart Trigger Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural comparison of fixed-period and gradient-orthogonality restart schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_m=\{k\ge1:k\equiv0\pmod m\}\) be the periodic restart set and let \(O_\tau=\{k\ge1:|g_k^{\mathsf T}g_{k-1}|\ge\tau\lVert g_k\rVert^2\}\) be the orthogonality-triggered set, with \(m\ge2\), \(\tau\in(0,1)\), and nonzero gradients. The periodic rule guarantees a restart at least once per \(m\) consecutive indices independently of observed gradients. The orthogonality rule has no corresponding iteration-gap bound without additional assumptions. For arbitrary gradient sequences the sets are incomparable: either \(P_m\setminus O_\tau\) or \(O_\tau\setminus P_m\) can be nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Periodic restarts bound the gap between restarts, while orthogonality triggers adapt to gradients; without extra assumptions, neither trigger schedule contains the other.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_m\) has bounded gaps, but generally neither \(P_m\subseteq O_\tau\) nor \(O_\tau\subseteq P_m\).

children.title: Conjugate-Gradient Coefficient Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Bounds and sign controls applied to nonlinear conjugate-gradient coefficients.

children.title: Coefficient Truncation
children.top_down_role: Magnitude limits imposed on nonlinear conjugate-gradient coefficients.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Truncation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interval projection safeguard for a tentative conjugate-gradient coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given finite bounds \(\beta_k^-\le\beta_k^+\), a tentative coefficient \(\widehat\beta_k\), current gradient \(g_k\), and previous direction \(d_{k-1}\), define \[\beta_k=\min\{\beta_k^+,\max\{\beta_k^-,\widehat\beta_k\}\},\qquad d_k=-g_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}.\] Equivalently, \(\beta_k\) is the Euclidean projection of \(\widehat\beta_k\) onto \([\beta_k^-,\beta_k^+]\). The coefficient is unchanged exactly when it already lies in the safeguard interval. This truncation controls coefficient magnitude but, by itself, does not guarantee that \(d_k\) is a descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clip the tentative conjugate-gradient coefficient to a prescribed interval before constructing the new direction; clipping alone does not ensure descent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\beta_k\in[\beta_k^-,\beta_k^+]\), with \(\beta_k=\widehat\beta_k\) whenever \(\widehat\beta_k\in[\beta_k^-,\beta_k^+]\).

children.title: Coefficient Sign Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Sign controls intended to preserve usable search directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Sign Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegativity safeguard typified by the positive-part conjugate-gradient coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a tentative nonlinear conjugate-gradient coefficient \(\widehat\beta_k\), define its positive-part safeguard by \[\beta_k=[\widehat\beta_k]_+=\max\{0,\widehat\beta_k\},\qquad d_k=-g_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}.\] Hence a negative tentative coefficient activates an immediate coefficient restart, \(\beta_k=0\) and \(d_k=-g_k\), whereas a nonnegative coefficient is retained. This safeguard prevents negative recurrence coefficients but does not alone imply \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k<0\); a separate descent test or suitable line-search and update-specific analysis may still be required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace a negative tentative coefficient by zero, producing steepest descent; retain nonnegative coefficients, while checking descent separately if needed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\beta_k\ge0\), and \(\widehat\beta_k<0\) implies \(d_k=-g_k\).

notation.meaning: Positive part, equal to the maximum of t and zero.

children.title: Coefficient Fallback Policies

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Fallback Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic fallback from an unsafe coefficient to a safe restart direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat\beta_k\) be computed from the chosen nonlinear conjugate-gradient formula and let \(\widehat d_k=-g_k+\widehat\beta_kd_{k-1}\). Fix \(c\in(0,1]\). Declare the trial unsafe if \(\widehat\beta_k\) is nonfinite, a required denominator is nonpositive or below its numerical tolerance, or \(g_k^{\mathsf T}\widehat d_k>-c\lVert g_k\rVert^2\). On an unsafe trial set \(\beta_k=0\) and \(d_k=-g_k\); otherwise set \(\beta_k=\widehat\beta_k\) and \(d_k=\widehat d_k\). The output always satisfies the required descent inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use the tentative coefficient only when its computation is valid and its direction passes descent; otherwise set the coefficient to zero.
assumptions_latex: Unsafe denominator thresholds are fixed before evaluating the update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\le-c\lVert g_k\rVert^2<0\).

notation.meaning: Direction formed with the tentative coefficient.

children.title: Safeguard Activation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Curvature or line-search conditions that motivate coefficient protection.

knowledge_statements.title: Safeguard Activation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential partition of coefficient acceptance, truncation, and restart regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_k=[\beta_k^-,\beta_k^+]\) be a nonempty closed bounded interval containing \(0\), let \(\widehat\beta_k\) be a tentative coefficient, and define \(D_k(\beta)\) by \(g_k^{\mathsf T}(-g_k+\beta d_{k-1})\le-c\lVert g_k\rVert^2\), where \(g_k\ne0\) and \(c\in(0,1]\). Apply the following branches in order. If \(\widehat\beta_k\) is finite, belongs to \(I_k\), and satisfies \(D_k(\widehat\beta_k)\), accept \(\beta_k=\widehat\beta_k\). Otherwise, if \(\widehat\beta_k\) is finite and its projection \(\bar\beta_k\) onto \(I_k\) satisfies \(D_k(\bar\beta_k)\), truncate by setting \(\beta_k=\bar\beta_k\). Otherwise restart by setting \(\beta_k=0\). Exactly one branch is executed, and the resulting direction \(d_k=-g_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}\) satisfies \(D_k(\beta_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First accept a finite admissible coefficient that passes the descent test; otherwise use its projected value if that passes; otherwise restart with coefficient zero.
assumptions_latex: \(I_k=[\beta_k^-,\beta_k^+]\) is a nonempty closed bounded interval containing \(0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one sequential regime is executed, and \(d_k=-g_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}\) satisfies \(D_k(\beta_k)\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection of the tentative coefficient onto the admissible interval.

children.title: Descent-Direction Theory
children.top_down_role: Structural conditions ensuring usable search directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Descent-Direction Theory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact descent and sufficient-descent criteria for a conjugate-gradient recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_k\ne0\) and \(d_k=-g_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}\). Then \[g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k=-\lVert g_k\rVert^2+\beta_k g_k^{\mathsf T}d_{k-1}.\] Consequently, \(d_k\) is a strict descent direction exactly when \(\beta_k g_k^{\mathsf T}d_{k-1}<\lVert g_k\rVert^2\). More strongly, for any fixed \(c\in(0,1]\), the sufficient-descent inequality \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\le-c\lVert g_k\rVert^2\) holds exactly when \(\beta_k g_k^{\mathsf T}d_{k-1}\le(1-c)\lVert g_k\rVert^2\). Thus coefficient safeguards can enforce descent by checking a scalar inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a conjugate-gradient recurrence, descent is equivalent to an explicit scalar bound on the coefficient and the previous direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k<0\) if and only if \(\beta_k g_k^{\mathsf T}d_{k-1}<\lVert g_k\rVert^2\).

children.title: Zoutendijk-Based Global Convergence
children.top_down_role: Global convergence through line-search curvature and direction-angle control.

knowledge_statements.title: Zoutendijk-Based Global Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Zoutendijk theorem with an angle condition yielding gradient convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), where \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k<0\), and each \(\alpha_k\) satisfies the Wolfe conditions with constants \(0<c_1<c_2<1\). Suppose \(f\) is bounded below on the initial level set and its gradient is Lipschitz continuous on an open neighborhood of that set. Define \(\cos\theta_k=-g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k/(\lVert g_k\rVert\lVert d_k\rVert)\). Then \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\cos^2\theta_k\lVert g_k\rVert^2<\infty.\] If additionally \(\cos\theta_k\ge\delta>0\) for every \(k\), then \(\lVert g_k\rVert\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Wolfe steps and Lipschitz gradients make the angle-weighted squared gradients summable; a uniform direction-angle bound forces gradients to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is bounded below on the initial level set and \(\nabla f\) is Lipschitz nearby.
Each step satisfies the Wolfe conditions with fixed \(0<c_1<c_2<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\cos^2\theta_k\lVert g_k\rVert^2<\infty\), and \(\cos\theta_k\ge\delta>0\) implies \(\lVert g_k\rVert\to0\).

notation.meaning: Angle between the negative gradient and search direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Update-Specific Global Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A transfer criterion separating generic globalization from coefficient-specific verification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider any nonlinear conjugate-gradient update \(d_k=-g_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}\) followed by a Wolfe line search. Assume the objective satisfies the lower-boundedness and Lipschitz-gradient hypotheses of the Zoutendijk theorem. If the particular formula, hybrid rule, modification, or safeguard for \(\beta_k\) guarantees constants \(c>0\) and \(M<\infty\) such that \[g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\le-c\lVert g_k\rVert^2,\qquad \lVert d_k\rVert\le M\lVert g_k\rVert\] for all generated indices, then \(\cos\theta_k\ge c/M\), and the Zoutendijk conclusion gives \(\lVert g_k\rVert\to0\). Update-specific analysis is therefore needed to verify these two inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any update family inherits Zoutendijk convergence once its own analysis establishes uniform sufficient descent and a direction-norm bound.
assumptions_latex: The objective meets the Zoutendijk lower-bound and Lipschitz-gradient hypotheses.
The line search satisfies fixed Wolfe conditions.
The update guarantees uniform sufficient descent and \(\lVert d_k\rVert\le M\lVert g_k\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\cos\theta_k\ge c/M>0\) and hence \(\lVert\nabla f(x_k)\rVert\to0\).

children.title: Quadratic Finite Termination
children.top_down_role: Finite-dimensional termination behavior on exact quadratic models.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Finite Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic finite termination of linear conjugate gradients on a strictly convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Ax-b^{\mathsf T}x\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric positive definite, and let \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\). Define \(g_0=Ax_0-b\) and \(p_0=-g_0\). While \(g_k\ne0\), set \(\alpha_k=-g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k/(p_k^{\mathsf T}Ap_k)\), \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), \(g_{k+1}=Ax_{k+1}-b\), \(\beta_{k+1}=\lVert g_{k+1}\rVert^2/\lVert g_k\rVert^2\), and \(p_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}p_k\). In exact arithmetic, some \(m\le n\) satisfies \(g_m=0\), and hence \(x_m=A^{-1}b\). More precisely, \(m\) does not exceed the degree of the minimal polynomial of \(A\) relative to \(g_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In exact arithmetic, standard linear conjugate gradients solve a symmetric positive-definite quadratic in at most n iterations, and no later than the degree of the minimal polynomial relative to the initial gradient.
assumptions_latex: Arithmetic and line searches are exact.
The directions use the stated linear conjugate-gradient recurrence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists m\le n:\ g_m=0\text{ and }x_m=A^{-1}b\).

notation.meaning: gradient of the quadratic at iteration k

children.title: Quadratic-Termination Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Effects of nonquadratic curvature, inexact search, or arithmetic error on finite termination.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Termination Breakdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the exact quadratic finite-termination mechanism when its structural hypotheses are perturbed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The finite-termination conclusion is not inherited by a nonlinear conjugate-gradient iteration merely because its directions have the recurrence \(p_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}p_k\). For a nonquadratic objective, the Hessian may vary with \(x_k\); for an inexact line search, generally \(g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}p_k\ne0\); and in floating-point arithmetic, previously generated directions need not remain conjugate. Consequently, the identities \(g_i^{\mathsf T}g_j=0\) and \(p_i^{\mathsf T}Ap_j=0\) underlying the quadratic proof can fail, so no dimension-only bound \(m\le n\) guarantees \(g_m=0\). This states loss of the guarantee, not impossibility of accidental finite termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonquadratic curvature, inexact line search, or roundoff can destroy the orthogonality and conjugacy identities; finite termination within n steps is then not guaranteed.
assumptions_latex: The iteration uses a nonlinear conjugate-gradient recurrence.
At least one of constant quadratic curvature, exact line search, or exact arithmetic is absent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_m=0\text{ for some }m\le n\) is not guaranteed by the conjugate-gradient recurrence alone.

children.title: Loss of Descent
children.top_down_role: Regimes where a generated search direction no longer provides reliable descent.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterationwise boundary between descent, orthogonality, and ascent for a nonlinear conjugate-gradient direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a differentiable objective \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(p_k=-g_k+\beta_kp_{k-1}\). The direction is a strict descent direction exactly when \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k<0\), equivalently when \(\beta_k g_k^{\mathsf T}p_{k-1}<\lVert g_k\rVert^2\). Loss of strict descent occurs at the boundary \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k\ge0\). If \(g_k\ne0\), every sufficiently small positive step decreases \(f\) when the strict inequality holds; this local guarantee disappears at equality and reverses to first-order ascent when \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An NCG direction loses descent exactly when its inner product with the current gradient becomes nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k\text{ is strict descent}\iff \beta_k g_k^{\mathsf T}p_{k-1}<\lVert g_k\rVert^2\); loss occurs when the reverse weak inequality holds.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The descent equivalence and first-order directional conclusion are mathematically precise and the failure-boundary kind fits, but no inspectable source locator is supplied.

children.title: Loss of Conjugacy
children.top_down_role: Degradation of curvature-based direction separation.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Conjugacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measured failure of successive directions to satisfy a chosen Hessian-conjugacy relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable, and let \(H_k=\nabla^2 f(x_k)\) be positive definite. Successive directions \(p_{k-1}\) and \(p_k\) are locally \(H_k\)-conjugate when \(p_k^{\mathsf T}H_kp_{k-1}=0\). Define the normalized defect \(\eta_k=|p_k^{\mathsf T}H_kp_{k-1}|/(\lVert p_k\rVert_{H_k}\lVert p_{k-1}\rVert_{H_k})\) for nonzero directions. Then \(0\le\eta_k\le1\), exact local conjugacy is equivalent to \(\eta_k=0\), and any \(\eta_k>0\) records loss of conjugacy. On nonquadratic problems this local condition does not imply conjugacy with earlier directions or under earlier Hessians.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Loss of conjugacy is quantified by the normalized Hessian inner product of successive directions; it vanishes exactly under local conjugacy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_k=0\iff p_k^{\mathsf T}H_kp_{k-1}=0\), while \(\eta_k>0\) signifies a conjugacy defect.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized local Hessian-conjugacy defect is internally correct, but this selected nonlinear conjugacy convention requires a source because competing conventions exist.

children.title: Descent–Conjugacy Interaction
children.top_down_role: Ways that degraded conjugacy contributes to poor directional quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Descent–Conjugacy Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic coupling of descent and successive local conjugacy in the NCG recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(p_k=-g_k+\beta_kp_{k-1}\), and let \(H_k\succ0\). If local successive conjugacy is imposed, then \(p_k^{\mathsf T}H_kp_{k-1}=0\) requires \(\beta_k=(g_k^{\mathsf T}H_kp_{k-1})/(p_{k-1}^{\mathsf T}H_kp_{k-1})\). With this coefficient, descent is still a separate inequality: \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k=-\lVert g_k\rVert^2+\beta_k g_k^{\mathsf T}p_{k-1}<0\). Thus local conjugacy alone does not algebraically imply descent unless additional relations control the two gradient-direction products; conversely, descent alone does not force the displayed conjugacy equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coefficient enforcing local Hessian conjugacy need not ensure descent; each property imposes a distinct scalar relation on the NCG direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local conjugacy fixes \(\beta_k\), but descent additionally requires \(-\lVert g_k\rVert^2+\beta_k g_k^{\mathsf T}p_{k-1}<0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic interaction is correct and property is an appropriate kind, but the local Hessian-conjugacy convention and its interpretation lack cited support.

children.title: Direction Recovery Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which line search, truncation, or restart fails to restore useful directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Direction Recovery Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restart criterion that restores a strict descent direction after an unacceptable NCG update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_k\ne0\) and let the proposed direction be \(\widetilde p_k=-g_k+\beta_kp_{k-1}\). Fix \(c\in(0,1]\). Accept \(\widetilde p_k\) only if \(g_k^{\mathsf T}\widetilde p_k\le-c\lVert g_k\rVert^2\); otherwise restart with \(p_k=-g_k\). The restart satisfies \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k=-\lVert g_k\rVert^2\le-c\lVert g_k\rVert^2<0\), so it recovers sufficient descent. This safeguard repairs the current direction but does not recover discarded conjugacy information. If restarting is forbidden and the proposed direction violates the acceptance inequality, this recovery guarantee is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rejecting an insufficiently descending NCG direction and restarting with the negative gradient restores a quantified descent condition, while discarding conjugacy memory.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted or restarted direction obeys \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k\le-c\lVert g_k\rVert^2<0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The restart calculation correctly restores sufficient descent and fits the recovery-boundary leaf, but the particular acceptance safeguard and threshold convention require a direct source.

children.title: Restart-Frequency Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Tension between retaining accumulated direction information and restoring robustness.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart-Frequency Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal comparison of periodic restart spacing with retained NCG memory and worst-case recovery delay.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider periodic restarts with integer period \(q\ge1\): set \(p_k=-g_k\) whenever \(k\equiv0\pmod q\), and otherwise use \(p_k=-g_k+\beta_kp_{k-1}\). Every block contains at most \(q-1\) recurrence steps carrying direction history, and any degradation detectable only through the periodic schedule persists for fewer than \(q\) further iterations before a forced restart. Hence decreasing \(q\) reduces the maximum scheduled recovery delay but shortens uninterrupted use of accumulated direction information; increasing \(q\) has the opposite effect. This deterministic tradeoff does not by itself assert that any particular period minimizes total work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Short restart periods limit recovery delay but retain direction history for fewer consecutive steps; long periods preserve memory longer but postpone forced recovery.
assumptions_latex: The method uses the stated periodic restart schedule.
A restart replaces the recurrence direction by \(-g_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maximum scheduled recovery delay is less than \(q\), while each block has at most \(q-1\) history-carrying recurrence steps.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The schedule-level counting claims are precise and principle fits the topic, but the periodic-restart convention and asserted tradeoff have no source locator.

children.title: Finite-Precision Direction Degradation
children.top_down_role: Numerical loss of direction quality in long runs.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Direction Degradation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Roundoff-induced loss of orthogonality and conjugacy during long conjugate-direction recurrences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In floating-point arithmetic with unit roundoff \(u\), computed recurrence directions \(\widehat p_k\) and gradients \(\widehat g_k\) generally satisfy perturbed rather than exact identities. For a fixed symmetric positive-definite matrix \(A\), define \(\delta_{ij}=|\widehat p_i^{\mathsf T}A\widehat p_j|/(\lVert\widehat p_i\rVert_A\lVert\widehat p_j\rVert_A)\) and \(\rho_{ij}=|\widehat g_i^{\mathsf T}\widehat g_j|/(\lVert\widehat g_i\rVert\lVert\widehat g_j\rVert)\). Exact arithmetic gives zero for the relevant distinct pairs, whereas nonzero computed values measure degradation. Because local recurrence errors can accumulate, neither exact conjugacy nor dimension-bounded finite termination follows from the floating-point recurrence alone; restart or reorthogonalization may be required to restore direction quality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Roundoff makes computed directions only approximately conjugate and gradients only approximately orthogonal, so long recurrences can lose quality and finite termination.
assumptions_latex: Computations use floating-point arithmetic with unit roundoff \(u>0\).
\(A\succ0\) and all normalized vectors are nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recurrence alone does not guarantee \(\delta_{ij}=\rho_{ij}=0\) or exact termination within the ambient dimension.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure phenomenon fits the leaf, but the floating-point accumulation and possible need for restart or reorthogonalization require a finite-precision CG source; the computed recurrence is also not explicitly specified.

children.title: Progress-Conditioning Signal System
children.top_down_role: Observable signals used to interpret convergence speed and anisotropy.

children.title: Optimization Progress Histories
children.top_down_role: Gradient and function-value signals distinguishing progress from stagnation.

children.title: Residual Histories
children.top_down_role: Iteration histories of gradient or first-order residual magnitudes.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Histories
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-indexed absolute and relative first-order residual diagnostics for unconstrained smooth optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For iterates \((x_k)_{k=0}^K\) of a differentiable objective \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), define the first-order residual \(r_k=\lVert\nabla f(x_k)\rVert\). The absolute residual history is \(\mathcal R_K=(r_0,\ldots,r_K)\). Given a scale \(s>0\), the relative history is \(\widetilde{\mathcal R}_K=(r_0/s,\ldots,r_K/s)\); a common initialization-based choice is \(s=\max\{1,r_0\}\). An entry \(r_k=0\) certifies first-order stationarity, while a small positive entry records approximate stationarity under the explicitly chosen tolerance and scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual history records gradient norms across iterations, optionally divided by a declared scale; zero residual certifies first-order stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable at every recorded iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R_K=(\lVert\nabla f(x_k)\rVert)_{k=0}^K\) and \(r_k=0\iff\nabla f(x_k)=0\).

notation.meaning: absolute residual history through iteration K

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the correct kind and the residual identities are precise, but the initialization-based relative scaling convention has no source.

children.title: Objective-Decrease Histories
children.top_down_role: Iteration histories of function-value improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Decrease Histories
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-indexed objective gaps and realized decreases for monitoring deterministic optimization progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For iterates \((x_k)_{k=0}^K\) and finite values \(F_k=f(x_k)\), define the signed one-step decrease \(d_k=F_{k-1}-F_k\) for \(k\ge1\) and the cumulative decrease \(D_k=F_0-F_k=\sum_{j=1}^k d_j\). If a finite reference value \(F_{\mathrm{ref}}\) is available, define the objective-gap history \(h_k=F_k-F_{\mathrm{ref}}\). Thus \(d_k>0\) marks a decreasing step, \(d_k=0\) no objective change, and \(d_k<0\) an increase. Under monotone descent, \((F_k)\) is nonincreasing and \((D_k)\) is nondecreasing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective histories can record values, stepwise decreases, cumulative decrease, or gaps to a declared reference value, with signs exposing increases and decreases.
assumptions_latex: Every recorded objective value \(F_k=f(x_k)\) is finite.
The gap history is used only when \(F_{\mathrm{ref}}\) is finite.

notation.meaning: objective gap to a declared reference value

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and telescoping identities fit the leaf, but no source supports the selected diagnostic conventions or reference-value semantics.

children.title: Progress–Stagnation Signatures
children.top_down_role: Joint historical patterns distinguishing sustained progress from limited improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Progress–Stagnation Signatures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed diagnostic predicates distinguishing quantified progress from simultaneous residual and objective stagnation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_k\ge0\) be a residual history and \(F_k\in\mathbb R\) an objective history. Fix a window \(w\ge1\), relative thresholds \(\tau_r,\tau_F\ge0\), and positive floors \(s_r,s_F\). At \(k\ge w\), define residual progress by \(r_k\le(1-\tau_r)r_{k-w}\). Define windowed stagnation by both \(|r_k-r_{k-w}|\le\tau_r\max\{s_r,r_{k-w}\}\) and \(|F_k-F_{k-w}|\le\tau_F\max\{s_F,|F_{k-w}|\}\). These are diagnostic predicates, not convergence theorems: stagnation can reflect near-stationarity, poor conditioning, an unsuitable direction, line-search failure, or finite-precision limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over a declared window, progress means a specified residual reduction; stagnation means both residual and objective changes remain below scaled thresholds.
assumptions_latex: \(w\) is a positive integer and \(k\ge w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequalities give explicit, scale-aware predicates for residual progress and joint residual-objective stagnation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the appropriate kind, but the predicates are conventional and uncited. For the intended fractional-reduction meaning, the residual-progress parameter should also be restricted to \(0\le\tau_r\le1\).

children.title: History Scaling Effects
children.top_down_role: Interpretive effects of normalization, plotting scale, and numerical resolution.

knowledge_statements.title: History Scaling Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformation laws showing which progress-history diagnostics are invariant under objective and variable rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widetilde f(y)=a f(By)+c\), where \(a>0\), \(c\in\mathbb R\), and \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular, with corresponding points \(x_k=By_k\). Then \(\widetilde F_k=aF_k+c\), \(\widetilde d_k=a d_k\), and \(\nabla\widetilde f(y_k)=aB^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_k)\). Hence raw objective decreases scale by \(a\), additive shifts cancel from decreases, and Euclidean residuals generally change anisotropically under \(B\). Ratios such as \(d_k/\max\{s_F,|F_{k-1}|\}\) are therefore invariant only when their reference scale is transformed consistently; unscaled histories from differently scaled formulations are not directly comparable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective scaling multiplies decreases, shifts cancel from decreases, and variable transformations alter gradient norms; comparisons require consistently transformed normalization scales.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable at the corresponding iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde d_k=a d_k\) and \(\lVert\nabla\widetilde f(y_k)\rVert=a\lVert B^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_k)\rVert\), so raw histories are generally scale dependent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The transformation formulas are correct, but the ratio-invariance claim is underspecified: a denominator involving the raw value \(|F_{k-1}|\) is affected by the additive shift \(c\), and 'transformed consistently' does not define a sufficient transformation law. A source and corrected normalization statement are required.

children.title: Stepsize-Direction Diagnostic Coupling
children.top_down_role: Signals revealing curvature mismatch, repeated rejection, or poor directions.

children.title: Stepsize Histories
children.top_down_role: Accepted, rejected, contracted, or expanded stepsize patterns across iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Stepsize Histories
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic representation for deterministic iterations with scalar stepsizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an iteration of the form \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_k d_k\), the stepsize history through iteration \(K\) is the finite sequence \[\mathcal A_K=(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_K).\] Its scale-free contraction ratios are \(r_k=\alpha_k/\alpha_{k-1}\) whenever \(k\geq 1\) and \(\alpha_{k-1}>0\). Thus \(\mathcal A_K\), optionally augmented by \((r_1,\ldots,r_K)\), records the accepted step lengths and their iteration-to-iteration changes without identifying them with displacement lengths \(\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|=\alpha_k\|d_k\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stepsize history records accepted scalar step lengths and, optionally, successive ratios; it remains distinct from actual iterate displacements when directions have varying norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A_K=(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_K)\), with \(r_k=\alpha_k/\alpha_{k-1}\).

children.title: Curvature-Mismatch Signatures
children.top_down_role: Trace features associated with steps or directions poorly matched to local curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Mismatch Signatures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observable mismatch between predicted directional curvature and the realized objective change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(s_k=\alpha_kd_k\neq0\), define the realized quadratic remainder and normalized curvature estimate by \[R_k=f(x_k+s_k)-f(x_k)-\langle\nabla f(x_k),s_k\rangle,\qquad \widehat L_k=\frac{2R_k}{\|s_k\|^2}.\] Given a model curvature \(M_k>0\) and tolerance \(\tau>0\), a curvature-mismatch signature occurs when \(R_k<0\) or \(|\widehat L_k-M_k|>\tau M_k\). If \(f\) has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, then \(|R_k|\leq L\|s_k\|^2/2\), so \(|\widehat L_k|\leq L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A curvature mismatch is flagged when the observed second-order remainder has an unexpected sign or differs relatively from the model curvature beyond a chosen tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable at \(x_k\) and \(x_k+s_k\) lies in its domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_k<0\) or \(|\widehat L_k-M_k|>\tau M_k\) constitutes the specified mismatch signature.

notation.meaning: curvature used by the step model

children.title: Ill-Conditioning Signatures
children.top_down_role: Zigzagging, scale separation, and flat-direction stagnation.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric positive definite with smallest and largest eigenvalues \(0<\mu<L\).
Gradient descent uses a constant stepsize \(0<\alpha<2/L\).
Claims of observed alternation or slow contraction apply to the corresponding nonzero eigencoordinates of the initial iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(1/L<\alpha<2/L\), every nonzero \(L\)-eigencoordinate alternates in sign, while its magnitude contracts; for large \(\kappa=L/\mu\), a nonzero \(\mu\)-eigencoordinate contracts slowly because \(1-\alpha\mu\) is close to \(1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact gradient-descent signatures on a two-scale positive-definite quadratic.

source_refs.locator: 8.1 From Gradient Descent to Subgradient Descent p. 195

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx\), where \(Q\) is symmetric positive definite with smallest and largest eigenvalues \(0<\mu<L\), and apply \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha Qx_k\) with \(0<\alpha<2/L\). In an eigenvector coordinate associated with an eigenvalue \(\lambda\), \[x_{k+1}^{(\lambda)}=(1-\alpha\lambda)x_k^{(\lambda)}.\] Hence, when \(1/L<\alpha<2/L\), every nonzero \(L\)-eigencoordinate alternates in sign while contracting. For the \(\mu\)-eigencoordinate, the contraction factor is \(1-\alpha\mu\); because \(\alpha<2/L\), this factor lies above \(1-2/\kappa\), where \(\kappa=L/\mu\), and is therefore close to \(1\) when \(\kappa\) is large. If both extreme eigencoordinates are nonzero, stiff-direction zigzagging and flat-direction slow contraction occur simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an ill-conditioned positive-definite quadratic, a stable stepsize above the reciprocal largest eigenvalue makes a nonzero stiff component alternate, while a nonzero flat component contracts slowly; both visible signatures require the corresponding initial components to be present.

children.title: Globalization-Numerics Failure Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Failures arising from acceptance policies, oracle inconsistency, and finite precision.

children.title: Stepsize Conservatism Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Repeated contraction or persistently conservative accepted steps.

children.title: Repeated Stepsize Collapse
children.top_down_role: Histories dominated by successive contractions or recurrent returns to very small accepted steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Repeated Stepsize Collapse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed diagnostic for recurring abrupt reductions in accepted stepsizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\alpha_k)_{k\geq0}\) be positive accepted stepsizes. Fix a collapse factor \(\rho\in(0,1)\), a window length \(W\in\mathbb N\), and a count \(m\in\{1,\ldots,W\}\). Iteration \(K\geq W\) exhibits repeated stepsize collapse when \[\#\bigl\{k\in\{K-W+1,\ldots,K\}:\alpha_k\leq\rho\alpha_{k-1}\bigr\}\geq m.\] This predicate distinguishes recurring abrupt contractions from a single isolated reduction; its parameters must be reported with the diagnosis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated collapse means that, within a stated window, the accepted stepsize falls by at least a stated factor on at least a stated number of iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed windowed count is at least \(m\).

A dedicated diagnostic source or explicit standard-field rationale is required.

children.title: Persistent Stepsize Overconservatism
children.top_down_role: Sustained acceptance of steps that are consistently too cautious for the observed local behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Stepsize Overconservatism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reference-scale condition for stepsizes that remain unnecessarily small.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) have an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and consider gradient steps \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_k\nabla f(x_k)\). Fix \(\eta\in(0,1)\) and integers \(K_0\leq K_1\). Persistent stepsize overconservatism on \([K_0,K_1]\) is the condition \[0<\alpha_k\leq\frac{\eta}{L}\quad\text{for every }k\in\{K_0,\ldots,K_1\}.\] The designation is relative to the smoothness-certified reference scale \(1/L\); it does not, by itself, identify the mechanism that selected the small steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stepsizes are persistently overconservative when every gradient step in a stated interval remains below a fixed fraction of the smoothness reference scale.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient with \(L>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_k\leq\eta/L\) for all \(K_0\leq k\leq K_1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is mathematically well defined and the scale 1/L is natural for gradient descent, but the label 'overconservatism' at an arbitrary fraction eta is a diagnostic convention not supported by the cited smoothness section. Dedicated support or explicit standard-field rationale is required.

children.title: Collapse-to-Conservatism Transitions
children.top_down_role: Regimes where an initial contraction episode produces prolonged cautious stepping.

knowledge_statements.title: Collapse-to-Conservatism Transitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic transition from abrupt contraction to a sustained small-stepsize regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\rho,\eta\in(0,1)\), a reference curvature \(L>0\), and a persistence length \(P\in\mathbb N\). A collapse-to-conservatism transition occurs at iteration \(t\geq1\) when \[\alpha_t\leq\rho\alpha_{t-1}\quad\text{and}\quad 0<\alpha_k\leq\frac{\eta}{L}\ \text{ for every }k\in\{t,\ldots,t+P-1\}.\] The first inequality identifies the collapse event and the second identifies the ensuing conservative plateau; both thresholds and \(P\) are part of the diagnostic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The transition consists of a sharp stepsize drop followed immediately by a prescribed number of steps remaining below a conservative reference threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A collapse at \(t\) is followed by \(P\) consecutive stepsizes not exceeding \(\eta/L\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The transition predicate is internally precise and belongs in the stated condition leaf, but no citation supports the chosen collapse-and-plateau diagnostic. Its thresholds and persistence rule are conventional rather than a standard theorem, so source support is required.

children.title: Objective-Gradient Oracle Consistency Boundary
children.top_down_role: Mismatch between reported function and gradient information.

children.title: Objective Information Inconsistency
children.top_down_role: Irregularities in reported objective values across evaluations, implementations, or precision settings.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Information Inconsistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Violation of deterministic repeatability or stated objective-error bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an objective oracle return \(\widetilde f(x)\) for a deterministic function \(f\). Under exact evaluation, objective information is inconsistent if two calls at the same input return distinct values. Under a certified absolute-error model \(|\widetilde f(x)-f(x)|\leq\varepsilon_f(x)\), two independent returns \(\widetilde f^{(1)}(x)\) and \(\widetilde f^{(2)}(x)\) are inconsistent whenever \[|\widetilde f^{(1)}(x)-\widetilde f^{(2)}(x)|>2\varepsilon_f(x).\] This test detects violation of the declared oracle model without determining which return is erroneous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective information is inconsistent when repeated deterministic evaluations disagree, or when their disagreement exceeds twice the certified absolute-error bound.
assumptions_latex: The objective oracle is declared exact or satisfies \(|\widetilde f(x)-f(x)|\leq\varepsilon_f(x)\).
Repeated calls use the same input \(x\) and the same declared evaluation mode.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact unequal returns, or \(|\widetilde f^{(1)}(x)-\widetilde f^{(2)}(x)|>2\varepsilon_f(x)\), refute the declared model.

children.title: Oracle-to-Oracle Disagreement
children.top_down_role: Mismatches among analytic, automatic-differentiation, numerical, stochastic, or surrogate information sources.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-to-Oracle Disagreement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-based disagreement between two deterministic implementations claiming to represent the same objective-gradient oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two deterministic oracles return \((f_1(x),g_1(x))\) and \((f_2(x),g_2(x))\) at the same query \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Given absolute tolerances \(a_f,a_g\ge 0\) and relative tolerances \(r_f,r_g\ge 0\), define \(s_f=\max\{1,|f_1(x)|,|f_2(x)|\}\) and \(s_g=\max\{1,\|g_1(x)\|,\|g_2(x)\|\}\). Oracle-to-oracle disagreement occurs at \(x\) when \[|f_1(x)-f_2(x)|>a_f+r_fs_f\quad\text{or}\quad \|g_1(x)-g_2(x)\|>a_g+r_gs_g.\] The diagnostic identifies inconsistency between implementations; without an independently trusted oracle, it does not identify which output is correct.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two purportedly equivalent deterministic oracles disagree when their objective or gradient outputs differ beyond prescribed absolute-plus-relative tolerances at the same query.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is supplied identically to both deterministic oracles.
Both gradient outputs use the same coordinates, ordering, and norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed predicate certifies implementation-level disagreement at \(x\), but not which oracle is correct.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative absolute and relative diagnostic tolerances.
Scale factors used to normalize objective and gradient discrepancies.

children.title: Finite-Precision Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Loss of measurable progress near arithmetic resolution.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational stagnation of a gradient update under floating-point evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\operatorname{fl}\) denote the implemented floating-point evaluation and let a gradient method propose \(x^+=\operatorname{fl}(x-\alpha g)\), where \(g\ne 0\) and \(\alpha>0\). Finite-precision stagnation occurs when \(x^+=x\), or when \(x^+\ne x\) but \(\operatorname{fl}(f(x^+))=\operatorname{fl}(f(x))\) for every admissible trial step generated by the globalization rule. In the first case no representable iterate change occurs; in the second, objective-based acceptance cannot measure progress at the available arithmetic resolution. Thus exact-arithmetic descent alone does not guarantee observable numerical progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stagnation occurs when every admissible computed step leaves either the represented iterate or the measured objective unchanged despite a nonzero gradient.
assumptions_latex: Arithmetic and oracle evaluations are performed in a fixed finite-precision format.
The proposed direction or gradient is nonzero before the floating-point update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact-arithmetic descent does not imply a measurable decrease or even a representable iterate change.
review_flags: No supplied source locator addresses finite-precision stagnation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the terminal container, and the two described mechanisms are plausible finite-precision failures. However, no source specifies the floating-point and oracle model, and the plain statement says every admissible step leaves the iterate or objective unchanged whereas the formal statement quantifies over every admissible trial only in the objective-equality branch. A numerical-analysis source is required before choosing the precise formulation.

children.title: Variable-Scaling Routes

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Scaling Routes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled-gradient route using symmetric positive-definite iteration-dependent metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given differentiable \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), initialize \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\). At iteration \(k\), compute \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), choose a symmetric positive-definite scaling matrix \(H_k\), set \(p_k=-H_kg_k\), and select \(\alpha_k>0\) by a descent line search. Update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\). Because \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k=-g_k^{\mathsf T}H_kg_k<0\) whenever \(g_k\ne0\), the scaled direction is a descent direction. Stop when \(\|g_k\|\le\varepsilon\), and return \(x_k\). Diagonal scaling and fixed preconditioning are special cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiply the gradient by a positive-definite scaling operator, globalize the resulting descent direction by line search, and stop at a prescribed gradient tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable on an open set containing the iterates.
The line search returns a positive acceptable step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(g_k\ne0\), the direction \(p_k=-H_kg_k\) satisfies \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k<0\).

notation.meaning: Iteration-dependent positive-definite scaling or inverse-metric matrix.

children.title: Momentum-Acceleration Routes
children.top_down_role: Escalation paths that target slow progress through momentum-based or extrapolation-based acceleration.

knowledge_statements.title: Momentum-Acceleration Routes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nesterov accelerated gradient route for smooth convex minimization with known Lipschitz constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient. Initialize \(x_0=y_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(t_0=1\). For \(k\ge0\), compute \[x_{k+1}=y_k-L^{-1}\nabla f(y_k),\qquad t_{k+1}=\frac{1+\sqrt{1+4t_k^2}}{2},\] and \[y_{k+1}=x_{k+1}+\frac{t_k-1}{t_{k+1}}(x_{k+1}-x_k).\] Stop when the selected stationarity, objective-gap, or iteration-budget criterion is met, and return the latest \(x_k\). The extrapolated point \(y_k\) carries momentum, while the gradient is evaluated at that extrapolated point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nesterov acceleration extrapolates from two iterates and takes a gradient step at the extrapolated point using the reciprocal smoothness constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed recursion defines the classical smooth-convex accelerated gradient route.

notation.meaning: Gradient Lipschitz constant used to set the step size.

children.title: Scaling–Acceleration Selection Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling–Acceleration Selection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic work-proxy rule comparing scaled gradient iterations with unscaled acceleration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the strongly convex quadratic \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx-b^{\mathsf T}x\), let \(Q\succ0\), \(\kappa=\lambda_{\max}(Q)/\lambda_{\min}(Q)\), and, for a chosen \(H\succ0\), let \(\kappa_H=\kappa(H^{1/2}QH^{1/2})\). Let \(c_s\) and \(c_a\) denote the respective costs per scaled-gradient and accelerated-gradient iteration. Under their standard quadratic iteration models, select scaling over unscaled acceleration when \[c_s\kappa_H<c_a\sqrt{\kappa},\] and select acceleration when the reverse strict inequality holds. Equality defines an indifference boundary. The rule compares predicted work to reach a common fixed relative accuracy; it is not a convergence guarantee for variable or inaccurate metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a strongly convex quadratic, compare per-iteration cost times scaled conditioning against acceleration cost times the square root of unscaled conditioning.
assumptions_latex: Both routes target the same fixed relative accuracy.
The standard condition-number iteration models are applicable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scaling is selected when \(c_s\kappa_H<c_a\sqrt{\kappa}\); acceleration is selected under the reverse inequality.

notation.meaning: Spectral condition number of the unscaled quadratic Hessian.
Spectral condition number after positive-definite scaling.

children.title: Scaling–Acceleration Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions where scaling or acceleration remains inadequate, unstable, or poorly matched to the observed diagnostics.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling–Acceleration Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete descent and stability failures caused by indefinite scaling or oversized accelerated steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Two sharp elementary failures delimit these routes. First, for a scaled direction \(p=-Hg\), descent requires \(g^{\mathsf T}Hg>0\). If symmetric \(H\) has a negative eigenvalue, choosing a corresponding nonzero eigenvector as \(g\) gives \(g^{\mathsf T}p=-g^{\mathsf T}Hg>0\), so \(p\) is an ascent direction. Second, for \(f(x)=\tfrac12Lx^2\), the zero-momentum gradient recurrence with step \(\eta\) is \(x_{k+1}=(1-\eta L)x_k\); it diverges in magnitude whenever \(\eta L>2\). Thus positive-definite scaling and step-size control are indispensable even before momentum is added.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Indefinite scaling can turn a scaled gradient into ascent, while a step exceeding twice the reciprocal curvature already makes the underlying gradient recurrence diverge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A negative scaling eigenvalue permits ascent, and \(\eta L>2\) causes divergence of the scalar gradient recurrence.

notation.meaning: Gradient step size underlying the accelerated route.

review_flags: No supplied locator explicitly supports both stated failure boundaries.
A source for the stability boundary and indefinite-metric failure is required.

children.title: Nonlinear Conjugate-Gradient Route
children.top_down_role: Large-scale route to richer directions without stored matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Conjugate-Gradient Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fletcher–Reeves nonlinear conjugate-gradient route with line search and descent restart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given continuously differentiable \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), initialize \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\), and set \(d_0=-g_0\). For \(k\ge0\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\) by a line search along \(d_k\), update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and compute \(g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1})\). Set \[\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{FR}}=\frac{\|g_{k+1}\|^2}{\|g_k\|^2},\qquad d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{FR}}d_k.\] If \(g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}d_{k+1}\ge0\), restart with \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}\). Stop when \(\|g_k\|\le\varepsilon\), and return \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fletcher–Reeves nonlinear conjugate gradient combines the new negative gradient with the previous direction and restarts whenever descent is lost.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable on an open set containing the iterates.
The line search produces a positive admissible step.
The update is evaluated only while \(g_k\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method generates matrix-free conjugate-gradient directions, with restart enforcing \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k<0\) after a failed descent test.

children.title: Curvature-Method Route
children.top_down_role: Escalation when first-order conditioning cannot be controlled adequately.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Method Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized inexact Newton route for escalation beyond poorly conditioned first-order updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable and initialize \(x_0\). At iteration \(k\), compute \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and a symmetric curvature matrix \(B_k\). Choose \(\lambda_k\ge0\) so that \(B_k+\lambda_kI\succ0\), and compute \(p_k\) satisfying \[\|(B_k+\lambda_kI)p_k+g_k\|\le\eta_k\|g_k\|,\qquad 0\le\eta_k<1.\] If necessary, increase \(\lambda_k\) until \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k<0\). Select \(\alpha_k>0\) by a descent line search and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\). Stop when \(\|g_k\|\le\varepsilon\), returning \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Escalate to a regularized inexact Newton direction, enforce descent, globalize by line search, and stop at a gradient-norm tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable near all iterates.
Each \(B_k\) is symmetric and approximates local Hessian information.
The regularized linear system can be solved to the prescribed residual tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The route uses curvature through \(B_k\) while regularization and line search control indefiniteness and globalization.

notation.meaning: Exact or approximate symmetric Hessian matrix.
Relative residual tolerance for the inexact Newton solve.

review_flags: Supplied conjugate-gradient locators do not directly support the regularized inexact Newton formulation.
